text:
sara: hey team — landing my first change today. quick orient: what branch names, PR size, and reviewers should I aim for? also any commit message format?
priya: welcome! :tada: short answers: branch -> feature/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short-desc. keep PRs < 300 LOC if possible. commit msgs: conventional-ish, e.g. `feat(fa): add caching for kv` or `fix(runtime): avoid npe`
jake: +1 to priya. For Redwood repos we try to keep logical commits and avoid giant refactors in one PR. If you need to, split into "mechanical" + "behavioral" PRs.
lina: also check CODEOWNERS — if your change touches infra/runtime code ping @lina and @infra-team for review. For api surface changes, add API review checklist in PR body.
sara: thanks! where's the branch naming pattern documented? I couldn't find it in the CONTRIBUTING.md quickly.
priya: docs link: https://redwood.dev/internal/dev-guides/branching (shortlink) — but TL;DR: kebab-case after the ticket id, max 50 chars. example: `feature/ENG-1283-pr-doc-links`
jake: CI expectations: run `./scripts/preflight.sh` locally (lint, mypy, unit tests). If CI fails on lint, you can fix and force a new run by pushing an empty commit: `git commit --allow-empty -m "ci: retrigger" && git push`.
sara: re: tests — some tests are flaky for me (timeout on ml-inference tests). what do I do?
jake: open the PR, mark the flaky test in the description, and add `@eng-oncall` as a reviewer if the flakes are infra-related. We can rerun the failing job via the CI UI. If it consistently flakes, we file a flakiness ticket.
lina: approval rules: 1 approving review from CODEOWNERS OR 2 reviewers if no codeowner. For infra or infra-runtime change you need @infra-approver.
priya: PR template checklist to paste in your description: 
```
- [ ] Summary of change
- [ ] Linked issue/ticket
- [ ] How to test locally
- [ ] CI green (or explanation of flakes)
- [ ] Docs updated (if applicable)
```

sara: great checklist. What about squashing? do we squash on merge or keep commits?
jake: keep history readable — small logical commits are fine. Default is squash-and-merge for tiny fixes, but for feature work keep commits unless you explicitly want squash. Follow the repo's merge policy (PR UI shows option).
sara: who do I ping to get a quick review?
lina: ping the team's rotation in the PR (e.g. `@team-runtime`) and mention `@lina` for priority reviews. If it's a small docs/typo change, @priya can usually merge fast.
ci-bot: [CI] build queued for commit 2f9a3b7 — lint: pending, unit-tests: pending
sara: one more: are there required labels? we use `area/*` and `type/*`?
priya: labels we try to use: `area/runtime|api|docs|infra`, and `type/bug|feat|chore`. Add `size/xs|s|m|l` too if you can estimate. Not strictly required but helps triage.
jake: also add `backport-needed` if it affects supported releases.
sara: awesome — this is super helpful. I'll open a PR and paste that checklist. thanks everyone! :heart:
priya: ping me in-thread once opened if you want a quick pass before requesting formal reviews.
lina: welcome aboard again, sara. excited to have you! :rocket:
